title: Match counts include rules with an empty assignment that the backend silently drops
description: Match counting for categorical (lines 142-147) and continuous/breakpoints (lines 152-168) only inspects the matching predicate (value equality / interval membership) and ignores whether the rule has a non-empty `assignment`. The backend (_rating.py _apply_banding) explicitly skips categorical rules with empty assignment (lines 88-92, `replace_strict` remap only includes non-empty assignments) and skips continuous rules with empty assignment (lines 124-126, `if not assignment: continue`). A rule that has a value/interval but a blank label thus contributes to the preview's matched count even though those rows actually fall through to the Default at runtime. This makes the preview over-report matches and under-report the unmatched figure for a partially-filled rule.
evidence: Frontend categorical: previewRows.filter(row => String(row[column] ?? '') === cat.value).length — no check on cat.assignment. Frontend continuous: matchesContinuousRule(val, cont) — bandingUtils only parses ops/values, ignores assignment. Backend _rating.py: categorical builds remap only when assignment is non-empty (line 91); continuous chain does `if not assignment: continue` (line 126). So {value:'London', assignment:''} matches 0 rows server-side but is counted in the preview.
